$comment: Allow-list for scripts/ci/check-anon-exposure-live.mjs — the sweep that reads
PRODUCTION and asks which relations the public `anon` key can reach.
Two statuses, and they behave differently:
approved      — a human ruled on it. Silent unless it disappears.
grandfathered — exposed when the sweep was built, never explicitly ruled on.
WARNs every run, and ESCALATES to a hard failure if it gains
rows while carrying an identity column.
2026-07-29: the 32 grandfathered entries are GONE, and not by being pardoned —
the Director reviewed them and every one was locked (anon grant revoked; see
migration 20260730000000_revoke_anon_on_grandfathered_relations.sql). The
exposure surface went 36 -> 4. Everything left here is a deliberate, explained
decision, which is the state this file is meant to be in: entries should be
rare and arguable, not a backlog.
Four of those 32 deserve a note, because they read as the opposite of what they
were. pde_certificates, pde_badges, pde_learner_badges and pde_reputation each
carried a policy granting SELECT TO public USING (true) — apparently to serve
the public certificate-verification page at /verify/[number]. They did not.
That page calls /api/certificates/verify, which resolves through
lib/services/certificates/verify-resolver.ts using createServiceRoleClient(),
and service_role bypasses RLS entirely. So the public policy served nothing —
while granting any anonymous visitor the right to enumerate EVERY learner's
certificates, badges and reputation. They were empty, so nothing had leaked.
Locking them was verified not to break verification: /verify/<n> still returns
200 and the API still returns a clean 404 not_found.
TO ADD AN ENTRY: state a reason a stranger can evaluate, and use `approved`
only when somebody actually decided. Guessing here disarms the sweep.

relations.name: castes
relations.reason: Read by app/student-form/[token]/ with the BROWSER anon client, by prospective applicants who have no account. Closing it breaks admission intake. Re-proven after the 2026-07-29 lock sweep: still HTTP 200 to an anonymous request, deliberately.

relations.name: community_categories
relations.reason: Same unauthenticated admission-intake path as castes, re-proven 200 in the same check. Closing it breaks sign-ups.

relations.name: institution_health_scores
relations.reason: Director decision 2026-07-26: aggregate, non-personal institution statistics, consciously left open. The rule applied was 'close everything holding personal data; review and consciously rule on the rest'.

relations.name: feature_usage_summary
relations.reason: Director decision 2026-07-26, same aggregate-statistics ruling as institution_health_scores. Counts of feature use, not rows about identifiable people.
